what_it_represents: Cross-species CDV transmission from lions to domestic dogs.
measurement_method: Bayesian state–space model; forecast comparison with and without lion-to-dog transmission.
role_in_analysis: Used to evaluate the impact of lion-to-dog transmission on annual probability of infection.
quantitative_result: Transmission from lions to dogs was negligible.
evidence_quote: This finding is consistent with the estimated lion-to-dog transmission parameter value [ω4 = 0.032 (0.00–0.20)] (SI Appendix, Table S5).

what_it_represents: A comparative index of host liability to parasite transmission across the wild-domestic boundary, based on specialized versus generalized parasite fauna.
measurement_method: A simple index was defined to compare host species according to parasite specialization versus generalization across the wild-domestic boundary.
metric_or_unit: Liability index (L).
role_in_analysis: Compared wild and domestic host species for cross-boundary parasite sharing.
quantitative_result: Goats had a liability index of 0.70, while horses had a liability index of −0.014.
evidence_quote: We define a simple index of liability to compare host species by the extent to which their parasite fauna is specialized versus generalized, i.e. crossing the wild–domestic boundary.

what_it_represents: Occurrence of argasid ticks in warthog burrows in the wildlife area compared with domestic pig pens.
measurement_method: Ticks were collected from 32 warthog burrows and 20 domestic pig pens; apparent infestation prevalence was calculated for each habitat.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of inspected burrows or pig pens containing argasid ticks, with 95% confidence intervals.
role_in_analysis: Quantitative comparison of tick occurrence across wild and domestic habitats.
quantitative_result: Infestation was 90.6% in burrows and ticks were found in 10% of pig pens.
evidence_quote: The apparent prevalence of infestation in the burrows (n = 32) was 90.6%, 95% CI (82.2–99.0), while argasid ticks were only found in 10% (2/20), 95% CI (3.1–23.1) of the pig pens inspected.

what_it_represents: The number of direct contacts between buffaloes and cattle simulated by the model.
measurement_method: Contacts were modelled as the presence of buffalo and cattle agents in the same cell at the same time; output variation was assessed in sensitivity analyses.
metric_or_unit: Number of contacts; percentage of output variation per percent of input variation.
role_in_analysis: Model output in one-at-a-time and Plackett–Burman sensitivity analyses.
quantitative_result: A 1% variation in buffalo movement input gave a 0.94% variation in contacts, and a 1% variation in cattle movement input gave a 1.07% variation in contacts.
evidence_quote: The outputs were the number of buffaloes outside the park and the number of buffalo–cattle con- tacts.

what_it_represents: Human-domestic pig interaction and contact opportunity.
measurement_method: State-level agricultural-worker data and county-level county-fair data.
metric_or_unit: State for agricultural workers; county for county fairs.
role_in_analysis: Interface-connectivity components (Cd-h) of the relative risk framework and map.
quantitative_result: Included as interface-connectivity data layers in the relative risk mapping.
evidence_quote: Agricultural workers (including animal caretakers and slaughterhouse workers) have the highest contact rates with domestic pigs

what_it_represents: Selected pathogens grouped by primarily close versus non-close direct-contact transmission routes in a domestic–wild ruminant setting.
measurement_method: Pestiviruses, BRSV and BoHV-1 were classified as mainly close-contact pathogens, and MTC as a non-close-contact pathogen, then evaluated in cattle and wild ruminant populations.
metric_or_unit: Categorical transmission route (close or non-close contact)
role_in_analysis: Structured the study hypothesis and pathogen evaluation at the interface.
quantitative_result: The paper found viral exposure in cattle but not wild ruminants, whereas MTC incidence in cattle and MTC seroprevalence in wild ruminants were similar.
evidence_quote: The wild ruminant population of DNP showed no seropositivity to the analysed respiratory viruses.

measure_name: Wild pig hunters and control personnel
what_it_represents: Human-wild pig contact opportunity.
measurement_method: State-level hunting and wild-pig-control data.
metric_or_unit: State.
role_in_analysis: Interface-connectivity components (Cw-h) of the relative risk framework and map.
quantitative_result: Included as interface-connectivity data layers in the relative risk mapping.
evidence_quote: Areas with more hunting have more wild pig-human contact

what_it_represents: A spatial and seasonal proxy for the wild-bird domain in relation to poultry-facility detections.
measurement_method: Weekly eBird relative-abundance estimates for mallards were obtained for 26.7 × 26.7 km grid cells and averaged by season.
metric_or_unit: relative abundance estimates; 26.7 × 26.7 km grid cells
role_in_analysis: Used as a population metric in spatial scans and to map domestic-premises detections in relation to seasonal wild-bird abundance.
quantitative_result: Poultry facility detections occurred in locations and during time periods when wild birds were in high abundance, although some high-abundance areas had no poultry-facility detections.
evidence_quote: Additionally, there were poultry facility detections in areas with high human population density and in locations and during time periods when wild birds were in high abundance (Figs. 4A and 6A), including near the GTA and Ottawa. However, conversely, there were areas with high wild mallard abundance and no poultry facility detections (Fig. 6A).
section: 3.5. H5 HPAIV-infected premises and wild bird detections

measure_name: Pestivirus antibody seroprevalence by wild and domestic ruminant host species
what_it_represents: A quantitative comparison of pestivirus exposure/infection patterns across sympatric wildlife and livestock hosts.
measurement_method: Sera were analysed for pestivirus antibodies by cELISA; positive sera were further tested by VNT.
metric_or_unit: Per cent seroprevalence and numbers of positive herds/flocks.
role_in_analysis: Compared seroprevalence between cattle, sheep and red deer using statistical tests.
quantitative_result: Seroprevalence was higher in cattle (59.4 per cent) than domestic small ruminants and wildlife; cattle seroprevalence was significantly higher than sheep and red deer (P<0.001).
evidence_quote: Results showed a higher seroprevalence in cattle (59.4 per cent, 13/13 of herds) than in domestic small ruminants (5.9 per cent sheep, 2/8 of flocks; 0 per cent goats of 4 flocks) and wildlife (10.8 per cent in red deer, 0 per cent in roe deer and 0 per cent in Cantabrian chamois).

measure_name: Movement patterns and activity-time overlap of free-ranging domestic pigs and bush pigs
what_it_represents: Potential temporal and movement overlap between domestic and wild pigs across the wildlife-livestock interface.
measurement_method: GPS/GSM tracking collars were used to monitor movement patterns.
metric_or_unit: NA
role_in_analysis: Descriptive preliminary assessment of pig movements and potential overlap; no statistical comparison or model is reported.
quantitative_result: There was an overlap between free-ranging domestic pigs and bush pig activity times.
evidence_quote: In addition tracking collars (GPS/GSM) were used to monitor the movement patterns of free-ranging domestic pigs and wild pigs. Domestic pigs were mostly active during the nights, early mornings and in the evening. The bush pigs were active from the evening and throughout the night wandering between game reserves and farmlands. There was an overlap between free-ranging domestic pigs and bush pig activity times and this might be a contributing factor to the ASFV disease epidemics.

what_it_represents: Cattle exposure to FMD virus from frequenting the buffer, an area used by buffalo and other wild ungulates.
measurement_method: Ratio of GPS locations in the buffer zone to all GPS locations over 24 hours.
metric_or_unit: Ratio of GPS locations recorded in the buffer zone to total GPS locations recorded over 24 hrs.
role_in_analysis: Explanatory variable in GLMMs of FMD serological incidence in cattle.
quantitative_result: Serological incidence was higher when incursions into the protected area were more frequent.
evidence_quote: The index is the ratio of the number of GPS locations recorded in the buffer zone to the total number of GPS locations recorded over 24 hrs.

what_it_represents: Farmer-reported contact between livestock and wildlife.
measurement_method: Questionnaire response included as a categorical predictor and compared across levels of satisfaction with dip tank activities using chi-square tests.
metric_or_unit: Frequency and percentage (95% CI) within satisfaction categories; P-value.
role_in_analysis: Potential categorical predictor of satisfaction with dip tank activities.
quantitative_result: The association was not significant (P = 0.907).

measure_name: C. burnetii seroprevalence by host species
what_it_represents: The frequency of present/previous C. burnetii exposure in wild and domestic host species sharing the study habitat.
measurement_method: Sera were tested for antibodies against C. burnetii using ELISA; positive, negative, and inconclusive results were classified using S/P% cut-offs.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence of exposure (frequency expressed in %)
role_in_analysis: Compared across host species using χ2 or Fisher’s exact tests.
quantitative_result: Seroprevalence was 33% in European wildcats, 24% in Spanish ibex, 19% in domestic sheep, and lower in the other tested species.
evidence_quote: Seroprevalence was 33% (95% CI 2·53–64·13) in European wildcats, 24% (95% CI 5·59–42·03) in Spanish ibex, 19% (95% CI 17·68–20·19) in domestic sheep, 1·6% (95% CI 0·21–2·98) in red deer, 1·4% (95% CI 0·00–3·02) in European mouﬂon, 0·2% (95% CI 0–0·727) in cattle, and 0·1% (95% CI 0–0·53) in fallow deer (Table 1).

what_it_represents: Two cattle farms each neighboring distinct but neighboring badger home ranges, representing potential contact mediated through neighboring badger social groups.
measurement_method: A D-edge was assigned when farm i neighbored sett k1, farm j neighbored sett k2, and setts k1 and k2 were neighbors.
metric_or_unit: Binary edge-type variable (presence/absence); odds ratio and attributable risk fraction.
role_in_analysis: Included as a binary explanatory variable in a logistic regression of whether an edge from an infected farm ended at a farm infected by the same molecular type.
evidence_quote: - A second level badger-mediated edge (denoted D-edge below) between farms i and j represented the fact that (i) farm i was neighbor of a sett k1 , (ii) farm j was neighbor of a sett k2 , and (iii) the setts k1 and k2 were themselves neighbors.

measure_name: Zero SNP differences between host species
what_it_represents: Genetically indistinguishable M. bovis isolates occurring within and between host species, used to indicate possible intra- and inter-specific transmission events.
measurement_method: Pairwise comparison of absolute SNP distances between strains.
metric_or_unit: 0 SNP differences
role_in_analysis: Used to identify possible intra- and inter-specific transmission events.
quantitative_result: Zero-SNP links occurred between red deer and wild boar.
evidence_quote: Links with zero SNP differences were identified within the same host species (cattle– cattle and wild boar–wild boar) and between different host species (red deer–wild boar), suggesting intra- and inter-specific transmission events.

measure_name: Standard tick counts by host domain
what_it_represents: The relative contribution of cattle and wildlife to maintenance of the total tick population on a mixed wildlife/cattle ranch.
measurement_method: Female ticks were collected and measured over four years from animals harvested for meat; counts used the concept of engorging female 'standard ticks' dropping fully engorged in the next 24 hours.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of total tick population
role_in_analysis: Quantitative comparison of tick-population maintenance by cattle versus wildlife.
quantitative_result: Cattle maintained approximately 75% and wildlife 25% of the total tick population on the farm.
evidence_quote: Based on standard tick counts, it was concluded that the cattle on this ranch maintained approximately 75% of the total tick population on the farm in comparison to 25% being maintained by the wildlife.
section: Wild Bovidae as maintenance hosts for ticks

measure_name: Proximity to nearest unprotected large water body
what_it_represents: Proximity to unprotected habitat attractive to wildfowl, representing greater potential exposure of poultry populations to wildfowl habitat.
measurement_method: Calculated to the nearest unprotected waterbody larger than 1 sq. km along a normalized scale of 100.
metric_or_unit: Normalized proximity scale of 0–100; one unit approximately 1.5 km.
role_in_analysis: Explanatory risk factor in multivariate logistic regression models of H5N1 poultry outbreaks.
quantitative_result: A unit increase in proximity was associated with a 7.7% increase in the odds of an H5N1 outbreak.
evidence_quote: By contrast, a unit increase in proximity (* 1.5 km) to the nearest unprotected waterbody was associated with a 7.7% increase in the odds of an H5N1outbreak.

measure_name: Coronavirus positivity in wild birds, duck flocks, and duck-area environment
what_it_represents: Comparison of coronavirus detection across domestic ducks, their environment, and wild birds.
measurement_method: Real-time RT-PCR positivity at flock and environmental-area levels, compared using chi-square tests.
metric_or_unit: Positive flocks or areas out of sampled flocks or areas; chi-square statistic and p-value.
role_in_analysis: Tests whether coronavirus positivity differed between domestic ducks, their environment, and wild birds.
quantitative_result: Two of five duck flocks and three of 16 environmental areas were positive; ducks and environment had similar positivity and both exceeded wild birds, in which no positives were detected.
evidence_quote: For coronaviruses, duck swabs were positive for 2 flocks out of 5 and environmental samples for 3 areas out of 16, but no duck flock was positive conjointly with envi- ronmental samples from their area (Table 1). Overall, the rates of coronavirus positivity in ducks and the environ- ment were statistically similar according to chi-square tests ­(X2 = 0.1, p = 0.7). As no wild bird was detected as positive by real-time RT‒PCR, both ducks and the environment presented significantly higher positive rates than did the wild bird taxa (­X2 = 530.2, p < 1e-10) (Figure 5).
section: Comparison of avian pathogens in the three compartments

measure_name: Sample location: within the reserve versus outside the reserve
what_it_represents: Comparison of rabies positivity among domestic dogs in the wildlife reserve versus dogs sampled outside the reserve.
measurement_method: Rabies brain samples were tested for lyssavirus antigen using the direct fluorescent antibody test (FAT); dogs were classified by whether they were sampled within or outside the reserve.
metric_or_unit: Percentage positive; odds ratio (OR) with 95% confidence interval; Chi-square test.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of dog rabies test positivity across reserve and non-reserve settings.
quantitative_result: Dogs inside the reserve had a higher positivity proportion than dogs outside it (65.3% versus 45.5%); OR = 2.26 (95% CI: 1.27–4.03).
evidence_quote: The odds of a dog sampled from within the reserve being positive for rabies was 2.26 times greater than for a dog sampled outside the reserve (95% confidence interval CI: 1.27–4.03).

measure_name: Host-associated CDV H gene phylogenetic relationship
what_it_represents: The genetic relationship of marmoset-derived CDV variants to dog-derived CDV sequences, used to assess a probable domestic-dog origin and spillover into wildlife.
measurement_method: Maximum likelihood phylogenetic analysis based on CDV H gene sequences.
metric_or_unit: Phylogenetic clustering; H gene sequence relationship.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of host-associated viral sequences to infer probable domestic dog origin and subsequent spillover into local wildlife.
quantitative_result: The marmoset-and-fox clade was most closely related to dog-derived sequences from Mato Grosso and Rondônia.
evidence_quote: This combined clade was, in turn, most closely related to dog-derived sequences from nearby states of Mato Grosso and Rondônia (GenBank: MT119972-77) (Figure 5).

what_it_represents: The number and proportion of a host's nematode parasite species shared across the wild-domestic host boundary.
measurement_method: Known host–parasite associations from databases and domestic-animal veterinary checklists were used to identify parasites reported in wild and domestic ungulates.
metric_or_unit: Number of shared parasite species and proportion of total parasite species shared.
role_in_analysis: Used to quantify parasite-species overlap between wild and domestic ungulates and to calculate liability.
quantitative_result: For goats, 29 parasite species were shared with wild ungulates and Pshared was 0.73.
evidence_quote: Shared (number of parasites shared with domestic ungulates); Pshared (proportion of total shared with domestic ungulates);

what_it_represents: The comparison between domestic guineafowls sampled in villages at the GMA periphery and wild guineafowls sampled at the Mulela plains-Ila forest interface.
measurement_method: Cross-sectional monthly sampling from November 2010 to October 2011, followed by comprehensive necropsy.
metric_or_unit: 148 domestic and 50 wild guineafowls
role_in_analysis: Grouping variable for comparisons of helminth infection measures between wild and domestic guineafowls.
quantitative_result: Domestic guineafowls had higher mean helminth species richness than wild guineafowls.
evidence_quote: Mean helminth species per host was 4.177 (SD: 1.654; Range: 1–7; CI: 3.91–4.44) for domestic fowls and 3.40 (SD: 1.107; Range: 1–5; CI: 2.92–3.88) for wild fowls. There was an overall difference in mean species richness between domestic and wild fowls (ANOVA F1,197 = 5.10, P = 0.025).

what_it_represents: Disease status of wild boar relative to cattle TB dynamics.
measurement_method: Estimated as the proportion of wild boars testing positive in the NWHSP relative to the total tested.
metric_or_unit: Proportion / prevalence (%) at county-year resolution.
role_in_analysis: Fixed predictor in risk-factor models of cattle prevalence, incidence, maintenance, and persistence.
quantitative_result: It was retained in the maintenance and persistence models, with odds ratios of 1.82 and 1.73, respectively.
evidence_quote: TB prevalence in wild boar was also included, estimated as the proportion of wild boars that tested positive in the NWHSP with respect to the total number of wild boar tested.

measure_name: Direct and indirect contacts among wildlife, humans, and domestic animals
what_it_represents: The annual contacts resulting from wildlife handling and wildlife trade across wildlife, human, and domestic-animal domains.
measurement_method: The article states that figures were compiled by the Wildlife Conservation Society from a variety of sources.
metric_or_unit: At least a billion contacts annually
role_in_analysis: Descriptive estimate used to characterize the scale of contact; not used in a statistical comparison or model.
quantitative_result: At least a billion direct and indirect contacts occur annually.
evidence_quote: All considered, at least a billion direct and indirect contacts among wildlife, humans, and domestic animals result from the handling of wildlife and the wildlife trade annually.

what_it_represents: The host-domain category distinguishing wild from domestic animals.
measurement_method: Host status was included as a sample characteristic in PERMANOVA of within-sample E. coli phylogroup composition.
metric_or_unit: Categorical: wild or domestic; estimated variation (%) and PERMANOVA P value.
role_in_analysis: Significant explanatory variable for variation in within-sample phylogroup composition.
quantitative_result: Host status explained 43.24% of total variation (PERMANOVA, P = 0.006).
evidence_quote: Permutational multivariate analyses of variance (PERMANOVA) of the differences between within-sample E. coli phylogroup composition and host and environmental factors identified host status (wild or domestic) and season (wet or dry) at the time of collection as significant variables, with host status having the largest effect, explaining 43.24% of the total variation (Table 1; PERMANOVA, P = 0.006).
section: RESULTS — Influence of host and environmental variables on within-sample phylogroup composition

what_it_represents: Farmer-reported livestock grazing adjacent to the protected-area boundary.
measurement_method: Questionnaire response included as a categorical predictor and compared across levels of satisfaction with dip tank activities using chi-square tests.
metric_or_unit: Frequency and percentage (95% CI) within satisfaction categories; P-value.
role_in_analysis: Potential categorical predictor of satisfaction with dip tank activities.
quantitative_result: The association was not significant (P = 0.907).
evidence_quote: Grazing adjacent to the Park 53 3 6 (2–15) 13 25 (15–38) 37 70 (56–80)

measure_name: Relative risk map for CoVs at the wild pig-domestic pig-human interface
what_it_represents: County-level relative risk combining pathogen availability in wild pigs, domestic pigs, and humans with interface-connectivity risk factors.
measurement_method: Risk factors were normalized from 0 to 1 and combined multiplicatively with equal weights.
metric_or_unit: Relative risk score, normalized 0 to 1 for each risk factor; county-level map.
role_in_analysis: Spatial risk assessment and mapping to triage surveillance resources.
quantitative_result: The paper presents a relative risk map and distribution of percentage risk values across counties.
evidence_quote: Each risk factor, Өr, is normalized from 0 to 1 using minimum-maximum normalization (i.e., with county values being relative to one another such that the highest score would be 1 and reflect the county with the highest risk factor score) to allow each risk factor to be considered equally.

measure_name: Host-domain-specific tick PCR sampling and rickettsial infection detection
what_it_represents: Ticks associated with wild animals, dogs, and humans were tested to characterize the potential movement of spotted fever rickettsia from wild reservoirs through domesticated animals to humans.
measurement_method: Nested PCR detection of the 17 kDa antigen gene in a sub-sample of ticks collected from wild animals, dogs, and humans.
metric_or_unit: 80 ticks tested: 50 from wild animals, 20 from dogs, and 10 from humans; PCR-positive ticks (number and percentage).
role_in_analysis: The host-domain categories defined the tick sub-samples used to analyse the presence of spotted fever rickettsial infections.
quantitative_result: Four of 80 ticks (5%) were positive; the positives included three Amblyomma ticks from wild animals and Rhipicephalus sanguineus from a dog.
evidence_quote: Out of 80 ethidium-bromide stained gel electrophoreses with PCR products (208 bp), only four ticks (5%) were positive for spotted fever infections (Appendix 1). These include three Amblyomma species: Amblyomma testudinairum taken from a wild boar (Sus cristatus cristatus), Amblyomma clypeolatum from a star tortoise, and Amblyomma javanense from a pangolin and Rhipicephalus sanguineus from a dog.

measure_name: Proximity of backyard farms to the Lerma marshes
what_it_represents: The spatially proximate setting of domestic pigs and poultry relative to the wild-duck marsh habitat.
measurement_method: Backyard farms were selected based on accessibility and proximity to the marshes; their location was reported relative to the marsh boundaries.
metric_or_unit: within a 6 Km radius
role_in_analysis: Sampling-frame criterion defining the wild-duck/backyard-livestock study setting.
quantitative_result: Nine backyard farms were located within a 6 Km radius of the Lerma marshes boundaries.
evidence_quote: Animals were sampled from ten different study units: wild ducks from the Lerma marshes, as well as pigs and poultry from nine backyard farms located within a 6 Km radius of the Lerma marshes boundaries (Figure 1).

measure_name: Minimum distance to open big game estates
what_it_represents: Spatial separation between cattle farms and open big game estates.
measurement_method: Hunting-estate perimeters were processed with ArcGIS 9.2 to calculate proximity of wildlife species near cattle farms.
metric_or_unit: Minimum distance (m); binomial form.
role_in_analysis: Predictor in the multilevel logistic regression model of TB new infection.
quantitative_result: OR = 1.45 [0.97, 2.16] for TB new infection.
evidence_quote: X38. Minimum distance (m) to open big game estates (b)

what_it_represents: Two cattle farms neighboring the same badger sett/home range, representing a potential badger-mediated contact between farms.
measurement_method: A B-edge was assigned when both farms were neighbors of a given sett; farm-setts were neighbors when a farm pasture intersected the badger home range.
metric_or_unit: Binary edge-type variable (presence/absence); odds ratio and attributable risk fraction.
role_in_analysis: Included as a binary explanatory variable in a logistic regression of whether an edge from an infected farm ended at a farm infected by the same molecular type.
evidence_quote: - A simple badger-mediated edge (denoted B-edge below) between farms i and j represented the fact that both farms were neighbors of a given sett;

measure_name: Transmission rate from herd to cell
what_it_represents: Transmission from domestic pig herds to wild boar cells.
measurement_method: Estimated by approximate Bayesian computation in the multihost spatio-temporal model.
role_in_analysis: One of the estimated transmission-rate parameters for routes between domestic and wildlife hosts.
quantitative_result: The transmission rate from herds to cells (β3 = 0.1631 (95% CI 0.0100, 0.3828)) was similar to that of cells to cells (β4 = 0.1315 ((0.0051, 0.3724)), though the betas for both the between-herd transmission rate (β1) and the transmission rate from the effect of the international border (β5) were 10-fold lower than others.
evidence_quote: β : Transmission rate from herd to cell Estimated 0.1631 (0.0100, 0.3828)

what_it_represents: A three-level spatial categorisation of cattle-rearing locations by intensity of wildlife-livestock interactions: intensive/high (zone 1), moderate (zone 2), and low (zone 3).
measurement_method: Five villages were purposively selected: two in each of the intensive and moderate interaction areas and one in a low-interaction location.
metric_or_unit: Categorical zone: zone 1, zone 2, or zone 3.
role_in_analysis: Independent categorical factor used to compare co-exposure distributions and as a predictor in Bayesian models.
quantitative_result: Cattle raised in moderate (zone 2) and high interface areas (zone 1) had a higher probability of FMDV and Leptospira spp. co-exposure than cattle in low interface areas.
evidence_quote: Cattle raised in moderate (zone 2) and high interface areas (zone 1) also had a higher probability of co-exposure to these pathogens than those in low interface areas.

what_it_represents: Comparison of RVFV neutralizing-antibody prevalence between wild buffalo and domestic cattle.
measurement_method: Sera were tested using virus neutralization test (VNT); prevalence was compared between species.
metric_or_unit: Seroprevalence (%), 95% confidence interval, and p value.
role_in_analysis: Species was evaluated in the total sample, including stratified analyses by region.
quantitative_result: The overall prevalence was significantly higher in buffalo (12.7%) than cattle (5.7%; p = 0.0016).
evidence_quote: The overall prevalence was significantly higher (p = 0.0016) for buffalo [12.7%, 95% CI (7.8–19.5%)] than for cattle [5.7%, 95% CI (4.3–7.5%)].

what_it_represents: Whether cattle from the interface had a history of grazing in the national park, representing movement into and exposure within a wildlife area.
measurement_method: Grazing history according to the owner (GNP or KNP) was collected for each cattle animal and categorized as grazing in Park or not grazing in Park.
metric_or_unit: Brucella seroprevalence (%) and logistic-regression odds ratio.
role_in_analysis: Additional predictor of seropositivity in a logistic-regression model restricted to female cattle; descriptive statistics were restricted to cattle from the interface.
quantitative_result: History of grazing in Park versus no history of grazing: OR 3.3 (95% CI 1.8–6.1; P<0.01).
evidence_quote: The results showed a non-significant association between antibodies against Brucella spp. and an increasing age of female animals and also a higher prevalence for those sampled from the interface areas. However, the results demonstrated a strong association (P<0.001) between antibodies against Brucella spp. and a history of abortion (odds ratio (OR)=35.8; 19.0<OR<67.6; χ2 =56.8; P<0.01) and that of grazing in the park (OR=3.3; 1.8<OR<6.1; χ2 =4.9; P<0.01).

measure_name: Spatial association between B. suis prevalence in wild boar and domestic pigs
what_it_represents: Spatial concordance between infection prevalence in the wild-boar and domestic-pig populations, based on prevalence estimates transferred between sampling locations of the two host populations.
measurement_method: Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) interpolation was conducted separately for wild boar and pig farm datasets; interpolated prevalence values from one host population were assigned to sampling points of the other host population, followed by correlation/regression analysis.
metric_or_unit: B. suis prevalence values; regression correlation with p-value < 0.05.
role_in_analysis: Used to investigate potential spatial associations and potential epidemiological links or shared environmental risk factors between wild boar and domestic pigs.
quantitative_result: A regression analysis revealed a statistically significant positive correlation (p-value < 0.05) between the spatial distributions of B. suis prevalence in wild boar and domestic pigs.
evidence_quote: A regression analysis revealed a statistically significant positive correlation (p-value < 0.05) between the spatial distributions of B. suis prevalence in wild boar and domestic pigs (Fig. 8).

what_it_represents: Comparison of pathogen exposure among domestic cats and the two wild felid species (bobcats and puma).
measurement_method: Host species was included as a predictor in a Bayesian hierarchical logistic regression of pathogen exposure.
metric_or_unit: Probability of pathogen exposure; regression coefficient and 95% CI.
role_in_analysis: Tested whether exposure differed across wild and domestic host species.
quantitative_result: Exposure increased from domestic cat to bobcat to puma (coefficient and 95% CI: 0.606, 0.061–1.111).
evidence_quote: As predicted, the probability of pathogen exposure differed among host species (Table 2, Fig. 2). Exposure increased from domestic cat to bobcat to puma (coefficient and 95% CI: 0.606, 0.061–1.111).
section: Effects of host species and pathogen mode of transmission

what_it_represents: The number of livestock in a space adjusted by the probability that the space is suitable elephant habitat.
measurement_method: A raster metric produced by weighting livestock density in each 1 km2 space by an E. maximus ecological niche estimated with a separate Maxent model using GBIF observations.
metric_or_unit: Weighted metric raster; livestock density per 1 km2 space weighted by elephant niche probability.
role_in_analysis: Environmental covariate in the Maxent model of anthrax suitability; ranked by permutation importance and evaluated in sensitivity analyses.
quantitative_result: It was the dominant feature delineating anthrax suitability, with permutation importance of 67.7%.
evidence_quote: The elephant– livestock interface was the dominant feature delineating anthrax suitability (permutation importance (PI) ¼ 67.7%).

what_it_represents: Cattle origin in an interface area versus a non-interface area.
measurement_method: Study areas and dip tanks were categorized as interface or non-interface; location was generated as a two-category variable.
metric_or_unit: Brucella seroprevalence (%) and logistic-regression odds ratio.
role_in_analysis: Predictor variable in logistic regression of cattle Brucella-seropositive status.
quantitative_result: Interface versus non-interface: OR 1.6 (95% CI 0.8–3.0; P=0.3) in the overall analysis.
evidence_quote: The seroprevalence varied from 9.6% to 11.2% for cattle originating from the interface areas while it varied from 5% to 8.3% for those originating from the non-interface areas.

what_it_represents: The landscape suitability of wild Ardeidae maintenance hosts.
measurement_method: An ensemble approach comprising boosted regression trees (BRT), random forests (RF) and generalised additive models (GAM) was used to estimate the landscape suitability of each of the 15 Ardeidae species; a composite measure was calculated from the mean of individual species suitability distributions.
metric_or_unit: Percent (%)
role_in_analysis: Covariate in the final inhomogeneous Poisson models of JEV outbreaks, jointly adjusted with domestic-host density and landscape features.
evidence_quote: JEV outbreaks were strongly associated with Ardeidae suitability (Table 1, Model 1—relative risk (RR) ¼ 2.77, 95% CI 1.15–6.69; Model 2—RR ¼ 2.44, 95% CI 1.02–5.86)

what_it_represents: Cross-species and cross-country virus transmission, including farm-to-wild bird and wild bird-to-farm transmission.
measurement_method: Estimated with a multi-type birth–death (MTBD) phylodynamic model from HA genome sequences structured by host type and geographical location.
metric_or_unit: Re; posterior median and 95 per cent HPD.
role_in_analysis: Quantified transmission between poultry-farm and wild-bird demes.
quantitative_result: Values representing wild bird-to-farm transmission were extremely low (median within the range of 10−3–10−2), whereas farm-to-wild bird transmission had medians of 0.1–0.4; the Czech Republic farm-to-wild bird estimate had a median of 4.6 (95 per cent HPD: 0.9–9.2).
evidence_quote: Overall, the between-deme Re estimates were much lower than the within-deme Re estimates, with extremely low values (median within the range of 10−3 –10−2 ) for those representing farm-to-farm across countries and wild bird-to-farm transmission (Fig. 4B, SI Appendix Table S3). Slightly higher values were found for those representing farm-to-wild bird transmission (median of 0.1–0.4). One exception was found for the between-deme Re estimate representing farm-to-wild bird transmission in the Czech Republic, with a median of 4.6 (95 per cent HPD: 0.9–9.2).

measure_name: Domestic aspect of disease versus diseases potentially shared with domestic animals
what_it_represents: Numbers of reviewed articles that mention the domestic side of disease compared with articles addressing diseases potentially shared with domestic animals.
measurement_method: Systematic review count of reviewed articles.
metric_or_unit: Number of articles (n).
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of representation of the domestic aspect among reviewed long-term wildlife-disease studies.
quantitative_result: There were 67 articles in which the domestic side of the disease was mentioned, compared with 454 addressing diseases potentially shared with domestic animals.
evidence_quote: Concerning the wildlife–domestic interfaces addressed in the publications reviewed, there are a relatively low number of articles (n = 67) in which the domestic side of the disease is mentioned (considering livestock and companion animals as ‘domestic animals’), compared with those addressing diseases potentially shared with domestic animals (n = 454).

measure_name: TB-positive status by combinations of red deer, wild boar, and cattle
what_it_represents: Municipal co-occurrence of TB-positive status across wild ungulates and cattle.
measurement_method: Municipalities were classified according to whether they were TB positive in red deer (RD), wild boar (WB), cattle (Bov), or combinations of these hosts in 2006 and 2007.
metric_or_unit: Number of municipalities; percentage of TB-infected regions with cases in more than one species.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive assessment of a potential multi-species interaction scenario; the paper states that host-variable interactions were not included in the final model.
quantitative_result: Many TB-infected regions presented TB cases in more than one species (44.19% in 2006 and 28.86% in 2007).
evidence_quote: Ciudad Real municipalities with this scenario are an exception (9 out of 113) and many TB-infected regions presented TB cases in more than one species (44.19% in 2006 and 28.86% in 2007) (Table 2).

what_it_represents: Geographic variation in water availability associated with risk of transmission among wildlife, livestock, and people.
measurement_method: Identification of geographic areas with varying water availability using information on bovine tuberculosis and brucellosis in livestock and wildlife.
metric_or_unit: NA
role_in_analysis: Used to identify areas where transmission risk may be high and in detailed models assessing effects on disease status.
quantitative_result: NA
evidence_quote: The HALI project has now identified bovine tuberculosis and brucellosis in livestock and wildlife in the Ruaha ecosystem and is using this information to identify geographic areas with varying water availability, in which the risk of transmission among wildlife, livestock, and people may be high.

measure_name: Feral swine serum-sample cross-reactivity to swine and avian IAVs
what_it_represents: Serological evidence of feral-swine exposure to IAVs associated with domestic swine and avian hosts.
measurement_method: Hemagglutination inhibition assays of 294 ELISA-positive feral swine serum samples against reference IAVs.
metric_or_unit: Number and percentage of 294 tested serum samples.
role_in_analysis: Quantitative comparison of feral swine antibody cross-reactivity against swine- versus avian-origin IAVs.
quantitative_result: Only 16 (5.4%) cross-reacted to one of the four avian IAVs, whereas 271 of 294 tested HI positive against swine and human IAV.
evidence_quote: Although 271 of the 294 feral swine serum samples tested HI positive against swine and human IAV, only 16 (5.4%) cross-reacted to one of the four avian IAVs included in the reference panel
section: RESULTS — Distinction between swine and avian IAVs

what_it_represents: Forest fragmentation and the edge between natural forest and human-modified habitat, treated as interface habitat associated with potential human exposure.
measurement_method: Gridded landscape predictor included in boosted regression tree models of cutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis occurrence.
metric_or_unit: Forest edge; edge density metrics (unit not reported).
role_in_analysis: Candidate landscape predictor in models of disease distribution.
quantitative_result: The edge landscape metrics did not rank amongst the ten most important predictors for either disease form.
evidence_quote: The edge landscape metrics did not rank amongst the ten most important predictors for either disease form.
section: Results — Environmental predictors of the recent past distribution of leishmaniases

what_it_represents: Free-roaming domestic dogs as an opportunity for contact between domestic dogs and wildlife in and near giant panda reserves.
measurement_method: A comprehensive survey in six village groups surrounding Liziping Reserve.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive evidence summarized in this review; not used by this paper in a statistical analysis.
quantitative_result: 64% (212/334) of dogs were free-roaming.
evidence_quote: A comprehensive survey in six village groups surrounding Liziping Reserve found 64% (212/334) of dogs were free-roaming(11).

measure_name: Reported contacts between cattle and wildlife
what_it_represents: Wildlife-cattle contact in grazing areas and at watering points in the CNP and OD interfaces.
measurement_method: A face-to-face farmer questionnaire, with contact defined as wildlife and cattle grazing together in an area the size of a football field.
metric_or_unit: Comparative proportions; P < 0.05.
role_in_analysis: Compared reported contacts between the CNP and OD interfaces.
quantitative_result: Contacts with wildlife were reported more frequently in CNP than OD, both in grazing areas and at watering points.
evidence_quote: Contacts with wildlife were also mentioned more frequently in the CNP than in the OD interface, both in grazing areas and at watering points (Fig. 2).

what_it_represents: Potential direct and indirect contact, and resulting transmission risk, between wild pigs and domestic pigs.
measurement_method: County-level backyard pig density data layer.
metric_or_unit: County.
role_in_analysis: Interface-connectivity component (Cw-d) of the relative risk framework and map.
quantitative_result: Included as a data layer in the relative risk mapping.
evidence_quote: Backyard operations often have low biosecurity allowing direct and indirect contact with wild pigs thus areas with higher backyard pig densities would have higher risk of contact transmission among wild and domestic pigs

what_it_represents: The spatial favorability of a group containing species typically considered HPAI reservoirs, specifically Anseriformes and Charadriiformes.
measurement_method: Species were grouped by cluster analysis based on highly related favorability distributions; a representative species from each cluster was used in the multivariable model.
metric_or_unit: Average importance (Imp = 17%)
role_in_analysis: Predictor group in the final multivariable outbreak-probability model.
quantitative_result: Cluster 4 had a moderate association with emergence of new outbreaks and average importance of 17%.
evidence_quote: A moderate association was also observed for Cluster 4, which accounts for the species typically considered reservoirs of the disease (i.e., Anseriformes and Charadriiformes), although its average importance is lower than Cluster 3 (Imp = 17%).
